newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MAS to introduce ticketless travel.
newsitem.headline: MAS to introduce ticketless travel.

text.p: Malaysia Airlines will introduce "ticketless travel" in April, which will include allowing passengers to pay for trips via a bank's automated teller machine (ATM), local newspapers reported on Friday.

Rashid Khan, vice president in sales at the national airline, told reporters at a tourism forum on Thursday that passengers paying by ATM would receive a confirmation slip which would be turned over at the airport for a boarding pass.
The Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) executive did not identify the local bank which will be involved in the ticketless travel, but said the system would begin on April 1.
Initially, the service will be available only for the airline's domestic flights, he said. Passengers using the ATM payment method would have to hold an account with the bank involved.

"In the first year, it (the new system) may not even reach five percent of total bookings, as time is needed to educate our customers," the Business Times newspaper quoted Rashid as saying. He said the new system was an effort to cut costs.
MAS carries about seven million passengers a year.
